retaliation

/rih-tal-ee-AY-shuhn/ - the stress falls on AY · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Retaliation means the act of striking back for an injury or wrong.

The seniors woke to a lawn of pink flamingos and understood at once: retaliation for the mascot they had borrowed in May.

Example

It began when the Hendersons reported the Yamadas' maple for overhanging the sidewalk. A week later, a complaint arrived about the Hendersons' trash cans; the week after that, their porch light; by August the two households were communicating entirely through the city's complaint line. Each filing brought retaliation in kind, tit for tat, all summer.

Retaliation is the exact word because it names the answering blow: harm returned for harm received. It always comes second — no first strike can be retaliation — and it points backward at a specific wrong. That claimed first wrong is what separates retaliation from this unit's malicious harm, which needs no excuse at all.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

reprisal: A reprisal is retaliation in a dress uniform — the formal, military-flavored word for an official answer in kind, delivered by governments, armies, and institutions through recognized channels. Retaliation is the all-purpose everyday word for the answering blow, at home in schoolyards and office politics alike.

payback: Payback is the slangy, spoken-aloud version of retaliation — what the answering blow is called in locker rooms and group chats. Retaliation is the word courts and newsrooms use for the same act; payback grins where retaliation testifies. Both come second, and both point back at a first wrong.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

forgiveness: letting the wrong go unanswered

mercy: choosing not to strike back even when you could

Where it sits · how much hurt is returned — pushback → retaliation → vengeance

pushback vs. retaliation: Pushback resists a move without returning the injury; retaliation gives the wrong back in kind.

vengeance vs. retaliation: Vengeance goes past retaliation — payback grown personal and outsized, and seldom finished after one blow.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back

Root — tali

Root — tali: of the same kind (Latin talis, "such")

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: act of

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (back) + tali (of the same kind — Latin talis, "such") + -ation (act of) = giving back in kind. Roman law's lex talionis — the law of like-for-like, an eye for an eye — sits whole inside this word: retaliation returns the same sort of blow it received.

The law of like-for-like

The law of like-for-like: Latin talis ('such, of that kind') survives in English only inside this one word and the lawbooks' lex talionis — the eye-for-an-eye rule. There's no everyday relative to spot; the old law itself is the relative, hiding in plain sight.

Strength Check

Word Choice

neutral / news-report

Retaliation is the wrong returned — always second, always pointing back at a first wrong, and often claiming to be proportionate. Courts and newsrooms use it precisely that way. When the answer grows personal, patient, and larger than the injury, it has become revenge or vengeance; when there was no first wrong at all, the honest word is this unit's malicious.
